description:
Handler functions state their result type and store bound once through shared aliases where the same spelling repeats across handlers, without renaming any existing type.

## Background

Every library handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` spells `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>` and, in many groups, the store bound `IssueStore + RepositoryStateStore` in full, and many build `Outcome::success(response)` from a bare response value. The remaining handler migrations will add more handlers with the same spelling.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One result alias names a handler's return type, and every handler uses it.
- [hard] REQ-02: One trait alias names the store bound the handlers share, and every handler with that bound uses it.
- [hard] REQ-03: A plain success outcome converts from its response value through one shared conversion, where that removes repeated construction.
- [hard] REQ-04: No existing type is renamed, and no command's JSON payload, human output or exit code changes.
- [hard] REQ-05: The change removes at least 30 production lines from `crates/jit/src` (default mode of `scripts/production-lines.py`). If the aliases cannot reach that by removing real repetition, the issue is rejected rather than met by cosmetic edits.

## Notes

Steward ruling (2026-11-04): shortening a name to save lines simplifies nothing, so the `CommandContext` name stays. Lands before the remaining handler moves so they start from the shared spelling. Part of the epic's net-reduction work (plan D-51).
title: Handlers share one result alias and store bound
